newsitem.title: USA: Hilton attacks ITT's $200 million sale of 5 hotels.
newsitem.headline: Hilton attacks ITT's $200 million sale of 5 hotels.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp., in a stinging letter to takeover target ITT Corp., Monday attacked ITT's proposed sale of five hotels to FelCor Suite Hotels Inc.

A portion of the $200 million deal, announced May 19, calls for ITT to receive a management fee for operating the hotels, which are scattered around the United States. But the management contract is severed if ITT's ownership changes.

"We view these change of control provisions as irresponsible and unnecessary," Hilton Chief Executive Stephen Bollenbach wrote to ITT's board of directors. "In this regard, Hilton is willing to purchase the five hotels at the same price.

ITT is the target of a $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid by Hilton, which is based in Beverly Hills, Calif. The rival hotel and gambling company launched the offer in January. ITT, based in New York, rejected the bid, calling it inadequate, then it began shedding non-core assets and refocusing operations on core hotels and gambling business.

ITT owns and operates Sheraton brand hotels and Caesars resorts and casinos. Hilton operates Hilton Hotels in the United States and promotes Hilton overseas in a joint venture with Ladbroke Plc. It also owns Bally's brand and Hilton casinos.

Bollenbach said Hilton would acquire the five properties on the same economic terms as FelCor, but would exclude the change in control provision making its offer "clearly more advantageous to ITT shareholders."

ITT quickly defended the FelCor deal, saying FelCor requested the change in control provision. A spokesman noted most of the recently announced management and franchise contracts between ITT and others include that same provision.

"The Felcor deal will be accretive to ITT earnings in 1998. Every asset sale that we have made since Jan. 27 when Hilton launched their hostile offer has been at exceptional prices and has added value for our shareholders," ITT spokesman Jim Gallagher said.

ITT has sold its stake in French telecommunications company Alcatel Alstholm for about $830 million and agreed to sell its 50 percent ownership position in Madison Square Garden Inc. for around $650 million.
The FelCor deal included hotels that are significantly smaller than ITT Sheraton's major properties and are considered to be mostly in secondary markets for the company.

Financial analysts expect ITT, when it has completed its asset sales, will launch a buyback offer for a large number of its common shares or issue a lucrative one-time dividend to boost shareholder support as it defends against Hilton.
Hilton's shares rose 75 cents to $29, ITT gained 37.5 cents to $60 and FelCor dropped 12.5 cents to $37.125 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
